title: Lambda Invocation Errors and Failed Invocations

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.5.1 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.5.1 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" metric_name="Errors"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.1_lambda_invocation_errors_1"
| sort -_time
description: Failed Lambda invocations surface runtime bugs, dependency outages, and misconfiguration before they silently drop user traffic or break downstream workflows.
value: Detecting lambda invocation errors and failed invocations early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable CloudWatch metric collection for the Lambda namespace (Errors, Invocations). Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws. Optionally correlate with Lambda application logs from CloudWatch Logs subscription. Alert when error rate exceeds policy (for example 1–5% sustained over 15 minutes).
visualization: Line chart (errors and invocations over time by function), Single value (error rate %), Table (FunctionName, errors, invocations, error_rate).
knownFalsePositives: Cold starts, retries, and a bad client sending junk traffic can all raise error counts without a code bug. We look at the share of invocations and we compare the same time last week before we assume the function is broken.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable CloudWatch metric collection for the Lambda namespace (Errors, Invocations). Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws. Optionally correlate with Lambda application logs from CloudWatch Logs subscription. Alert when error rate exceeds policy (for example 1–5% sustained over 15 minutes).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" metric_name="Errors"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.1_lambda_invocation_errors_1"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect lambda invocation errors and failed invocations. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_1_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (errors and invocations over time by function), Single value (error rate %), Table (FunctionName, errors, invocations, error_rate)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of lambda invocation errors and failed invocations so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
